programmes.summary: All 17 Mozambique LNG carrier slots (HD Hyundai Samho x9, Samsung Heavy Industries x8; MOL/NYK and Maran Gas/NYK as owners) remain at Letter-of-Intent/reservation stage, first signed in 2020. TotalEnergies restarted the onshore/offshore project in Jan 2026 after lifting force majeure (Nov 2025), but as of the most recent reporting found (17-Jul-2026 iMarine; 1-Jul-2026 Korean press) the shipbuilding order confirmation deadline had been pushed back again, to Q3/September 2026 -- i.e., to right around the present date -- with no report yet confirming either a binding contract signature or a lapse/cancellation. Per-vessel prices are reported to have risen from ~$180m (2020 LOI) to over $260m in current market terms, which would apply if/when the LOI converts. No evidence found of any part of this programme already appearing in the backend as an on-order row (checked Shipowner=MOL/NYK/Maran Gas x Shipbuilder=HD Hyundai Samho/Samsung Heavy on-order entries with Mozambique/TotalEnergies context -- none found), so all 17 rows are kept as proposed placeholders, unchanged.

programmes.summary: Woodside's Louisiana LNG carrier tender (TradeWinds reported 16-20 vessels needed) has partly converted. TradeWinds (31-Mar-2026) reported Maran Gas Maritime and Seapeak as preferred bidders, each expected to take at least a pair. Maran Gas firmed 2 x 174,000-cbm newbuildings at Hanwha Ocean on 24-Mar-2026 (~$501-505m) -- already in the backend as on-order rows 1141-1142 -- but the Woodside charter link for that pair is only TradeWinds' hedged 'it is understood', never company-confirmed, so the backend correctly does not attribute those two rows' Operator/charterer to Woodside. Seapeak's conversion is fully confirmed: its Q1 2026 earnings release states it signed contracts (May 2026) for 3 x 174,000-cbm X-DF LNG carriers at Samsung Heavy Industries, $756m total, delivery 1H 2029, against long-term charters explicitly named as Woodside Energy -- already captured in the backend as on-order rows 1165-1167. Because those 3 converted vessels are already on-order elsewhere in the backend, 3 of the 16 generic 'Woodside Energy NN' proposed placeholder rows are now duplicates and should be deleted; the remaining 13 placeholders stay proposed pending confirmation of the rest of the 16-20-vessel programme.

evidence.quote: TradeWinds understands that both Maria Angelioussis-led Maran Gas Maritime and shipowner Seapeak have been selected to provide at least one pair each against charters with Woodside... Priced at just over $250m each, the vessels are scheduled for delivery by mid-2029.

Seapeak has ordered three LNG carriers worth $756m at Samsung Heavy Industries against long-term charter contracts with Australia's Woodside Energy... The 174,000-cbm vessels, to be fitted with low-pressure X-DF propulsion systems, are due for delivery in the first half of 2029.
Seapeak orders more LNG carriers at Samsung Heavy
Seapeak grows LNG orderbook with $756m Samsung Heavy trio
Greece's Maran Gas, the gas shipping unit of Angelicoussis, has ordered two liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers from South Korean shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean.

programmes.summary: The 'Equinor 4' placeholder represents the unclaimed remainder of a Dec-2025 TradeWinds-reported tender in which Equinor shortlisted five owners (BW LNG, Knutsen, Maran Gas Maritime, Seapeak, NYK) for 'up to four' new LNG carriers to be built at Hanwha Ocean. Three of those four slots already converted: Knutsen signed for 3 vessels on 18-Dec-2025 (174,000 cbm, Hanwha Ocean, delivery 2028), already captured in the backend as on-order rows 1105-1107 ('Equinor 1/2/3', Shipowner Knutsen OAS). No evidence was found (searched through mid-Sep-2026, including Korean-press and TradeWinds/LNG Prime coverage of Hanwha Ocean's 2026 order intake) that the remaining 4th slot has been awarded to any of the other shortlisted owners (BW LNG, Maran Gas Maritime, Seapeak, NYK), nor that the tender has been cancelled. BW LNG's 2026 Equinor-chartered deliveries (BW Nivalis, Feb-2026; BW Borealis, Mar-2026) are pre-existing newbuildings from an earlier order, unrelated to this tender's remaining slot. Row 1186 is not a duplicate of the already-converted rows 1105-1107 (those are separate rows), so no deletion action applies -- it is simply the genuinely still-open portion of the tender. Keep as proposed.
